title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by providing safe autotuned defaults for request batching and KV-prefix caching, adding quantization profile support in the model registry, and shipping a unit-economics dashboard and CLI tooling to help customers visualize cost-impact. This PR implements: 1) an autotuner that recommends batch_size and batch_latency targets per model based on observed sequence length distribution and tail latency SLOs, 2) default KV cache sizing and prefix caching policies that are conservative by default but can be unlocked for aggressive customers, 3) integration of quantization profiles into the model registry (int8 and mixed precision presets) with compatibility checks and automated fallback rules, 4) a unit-econ service and console widgets that expose estimated cost/token and projected monthly spend under selected profiles, and 5) a small CLI (redwood uecon) to run local workload sims. Checklist: - [x] autotuner core logic and tests - [x] cache policy defaults and feature flag - [x] quant profiles schema + migration - [x] model-registry compatibility checks - [x] unit-econ service + console panel - [x] CLI tooling and docs - [x] e2e perf validation against standard benchmark suite - [x] rollout plan (gradual: opt-in feature flag -> default off -> enable for low-risk customers) Impact: expected 10-35% cost reduction for batched workloads; conservative defaults chosen to avoid correctness regressions. Rollout notes: feature gated; will enable metric monitoring and automatic rollback if quality regression or latency SLO violation detected.

Priya Nair: We use EWMA for sequence length distributions and require a minimum sample size and a cooldown window before changes are applied; added tests to cover noisy inputs
Samir Patel: Can we add an explicit opt-out tag per deployment to avoid applying defaults to latency-critical customers?
Priya Nair: Added per-deployment opt-out label and a migration that preserves existing configs
Ava Martinez: The quant profile migration needs a migration plan for dedicated customers who pin old model versions
Priya Nair: Migration plan added to docs and to model-registry migration: older pinned versions keep previous behavior until owner approves upgrade
QA Bot: e2e suite reported 2 regressions in a specific long-context workload; author fixed handling of KV cache with mixed-precision and re-ran benchmarks
Jordan Lee: Approved after e2e green and small test additions
ci_history_notes: Initial e2e run surfaced a regression on long-context KV cache + mixed-precision path; fix applied and retried. All checks green on re-run.
perf_results_summary: Standard bench suite (conversation+completion mix) shows median latency change +2% and 20-30% reduction in cost-per-1k-tokens for batched workloads; tail latency unchanged for 99th percentile under default conservative settings.
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce unit costs, quantization profile support in model registry with safe fallback, and unit-economics dashboard + CLI for cost projections. Feature is feature-flagged and will be rolled out gradually.
rollout_plan: feature-flagged -> opt-in test on canary customers -> enable for low-risk orgs after 2 weeks of stability -> default enable for new customers after monitoring thresholds
security_considerations: Quant profiles validated server-side; no secrets added. Unit-econ service uses aggregated telemetry and respects PII filters. Audit logging added for migration and automatic upgrades.
backport_notes: Backport to release/2026-02 for hotfix branch not required; changes are behind feature flags and will be cherry-picked if customers request earlier availability.
notes_for_release_manager: Monitor uecon dashboard for unexpected spend changes and set alert thresholds. Watch 99p latency and quality regression alerts during rollout window.
changelog_entry: 2026-02-25: Add autotune batching/caching defaults, quant profiles, unit-econ tooling (feature-flagged).
testing_steps: Run tests: pytest -k autotuner; run e2e bench: ./tools/run_bench --suite uecon_suite; verify uecon panel shows projected cost change; enable feature flag on staging and monitor metrics for 48h
authors_notes: This PR bundles infra+runtime+frontend changes to provide an end-to-end cost optimization flow. Kept defaults conservative to avoid UX surprises. Open to follow-up PRs to expand quant presets and add per-route heuristics.
customer_impact: Low risk by default (feature off). Customers who opt-in should see immediate unit-cost improvements for batched workloads; documented rollback steps included.
notes: See docs/ops/autotune_rollout.md for migration/checklist and web/console/uecon_panel.tsx for UX details
